-- Test point-in-time recovery capability
-- 1. Create test scenario
BEGIN;
INSERT INTO test_events (event_time, description) VALUES (NOW(), 'Pre-recovery baseline');
SELECT pg_sleep(10);  -- Wait 10 seconds
INSERT INTO test_events (event_time, description) VALUES (NOW(), 'Event to recover to');
SELECT pg_sleep(10);
INSERT INTO test_events (event_time, description) VALUES (NOW(), 'Event to lose');
COMMIT;

-- 2. Record recovery point
SELECT NOW() as recovery_point;
-- Result: '2024-01-15 14:30:00'

-- 3. Simulate disaster
DROP TABLE test_events;

-- 4. Execute point-in-time recovery
-- PostgreSQL example:
pg_restore --dbname=recovery_db --clean --create \
  --recovery-target-time="2024-01-15 14:30:00" \
  latest_backup.dump

-- 5. Validate recovery
SELECT 
    COUNT(*) as recovered_events,
    MAX(event_time) as latest_event,
    MIN(event_time) as earliest_event,
    STRING_AGG(description, ', ') as events
FROM test_events;
-- Should show 2 events, max time <= recovery point

-- 6. Verify no data beyond recovery point
SELECT 
    'Post-recovery data leak' as test,
    COUNT(*) as events_beyond_recovery
FROM test_events
WHERE event_time > '2024-01-15 14:30:00';
-- Should be 0

content.caption: Automated Backup Health Dashboard
content.code:
-- Comprehensive backup health monitoring
CREATE TABLE backup_health_dashboard AS
WITH backup_metrics AS (
    SELECT 
        backup_id,
        backup_type,
        start_time,
        end_time,
        EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (end_time - start_time)) as duration_seconds,
        backup_size_gb,
        success,
        verification_status
    FROM backup_log
    WHERE backup_time > CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '30 days'
),
recovery_metrics AS (
    SELECT 
        test_id,
        test_scenario,
        recovery_start,
        recovery_end,
        EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (recovery_end - recovery_start)) as recovery_seconds,
        data_loss_minutes,
        success as recovery_success
    FROM recovery_tests
    WHERE test_date > CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '90 days'
),
sla_compliance AS (
    SELECT 
        'RTO Compliance' as metric,
        COUNT(*) as total_tests,
        SUM(CASE WHEN recovery_seconds <= 240 * 60 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as compliant_tests,  -- 4 hours
        ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN recovery_seconds <= 240 * 60 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(*), 2) as compliance_rate
    FROM recovery_metrics
    WHERE recovery_success = true
    UNION ALL
    SELECT 
        'RPO Compliance',
        COUNT(*),
        SUM(CASE WHEN data_loss_minutes <= 15 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END),  -- 15 minutes
        ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN data_loss_minutes <= 15 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(*), 2)
    FROM recovery_metrics
    WHERE recovery_success = true
)
SELECT 
    -- Backup success rate
    (SELECT 
        ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN success THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(*), 2)
     FROM backup_metrics) as backup_success_rate,
    
    -- Average backup duration
    (SELECT 
        ROUND(AVG(duration_seconds) / 60, 2)
     FROM backup_metrics 
     WHERE success = true) as avg_backup_minutes,
    
    -- Verification success rate
    (SELECT 
        ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN verification_status = 'verified' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(*), 2)
     FROM backup_metrics 
     WHERE success = true) as verification_rate,
    
    -- Recovery success rate
    (SELECT 
        ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN recovery_success THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(*), 2)
     FROM recovery_metrics) as recovery_success_rate,
    
    -- SLA compliance rates
    (SELECT compliance_rate FROM sla_compliance WHERE metric = 'RTO Compliance') as rto_compliance,
    (SELECT compliance_rate FROM sla_compliance WHERE metric = 'RPO Compliance') as rpo_compliance,
    
    -- Days since last full test
    (SELECT 
        EXTRACT(DAY FROM NOW() - MAX(test_date))
     FROM recovery_tests 
     WHERE test_scenario = 'Full Disaster Recovery') as days_since_full_test,
    
    -- Critical backup age
    (SELECT 
        EXTRACT(HOUR FROM NOW() - MAX(backup_time))
     FROM backup_log 
     WHERE backup_type = 'critical' 
       AND success = true) as hours_since_critical_backup;

-- Generate alerts
SELECT 
    CASE 
        WHEN backup_success_rate < 99 THEN '⚠️ Backup success rate below 99%'
        WHEN verification_rate < 95 THEN '⚠️ Verification rate below 95%'
        WHEN recovery_success_rate < 90 THEN '🚨 Recovery success rate below 90%'
        WHEN rto_compliance < 95 THEN '🚨 RTO compliance below 95%'
        WHEN rpo_compliance < 95 THEN '🚨 RPO compliance below 95%'
        WHEN days_since_full_test > 30 THEN '⚠️ Full recovery test overdue'
        WHEN hours_since_critical_backup > 24 THEN '⚠️ Critical backup overdue'
        ELSE '✅ All systems nominal'
    END as alert_status
FROM backup_health_dashboard;

content.caption: Automated Recovery Testing Framework
content.code:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Automated Recovery Testing Framework
Simulates disasters and validates recovery
"""

import psycopg2
import time
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
from typing import Dict, List
from dataclasses import dataclass
import subprocess
import sys

@dataclass
class RecoveryTestResult:
    test_scenario: str
    start_time: datetime
    end_time: datetime
    recovery_time_seconds: float
    data_loss_minutes: float
    success: bool
    verification_details: str
    errors: List[str]

class RecoveryTester:
    def __init__(self, production_conn_str: str, backup_location: str):
        self.prod_conn = psycopg2.connect(production_conn_str)
        self.backup_location = backup_location
        self.results: List[RecoveryTestResult] = []
    
    def test_full_recovery(self) -> RecoveryTestResult:
        """Test complete database recovery"""
        print("🚀 Testing Full Database Recovery...")
        start_time = datetime.now()
        errors = []
        
        try:
            # 1. Get pre-recovery state
            pre_recovery_state = self._capture_production_state()
            
            # 2. Simulate disaster (in test environment)
            print("  Simulating database loss...")
            test_db_name = f"recovery_test_{int(time.time())}"
            
            # 3. Restore from backup
            print(f"  Restoring to test database: {test_db_name}")
            restore_start = time.time()
            
            # Example PostgreSQL restore command
            cmd = [
                'pg_restore',
                '--dbname', test_db_name,
                '--clean',
                '--create',
                self.backup_location
            ]
            result = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True)
            
            if result.returncode != 0:
                errors.append(f"Restore failed: {result.stderr}")
                raise Exception(f"Restore failed: {result.stderr}")
            
            restore_time = time.time() - restore_start
            print(f"  Restore completed in {restore_time:.1f} seconds")
            
            # 4. Verify restored data
            print("  Verifying restored data...")
            verification = self._verify_restored_data(test_db_name, pre_recovery_state)
            
            # 5. Test application connectivity
            print("  Testing application functionality...")
            app_test = self._test_application_functionality(test_db_name)
            
            if not app_test["success"]:
                errors.append(f"Application test failed: {app_test['details']}")
            
            success = len(errors) == 0
            verification_details = f"Restore: {restore_time:.1f}s, Verification: {verification['status']}"
            
            if app_test["success"]:
                verification_details += f", Application: OK"
            
        except Exception as e:
            errors.append(str(e))
            success = False
            verification_details = f"Error: {e}"
        
        end_time = datetime.now()
        recovery_time = (end_time - start_time).total_seconds()
        
        # Calculate data loss (time since last backup)
        backup_age = self._get_backup_age()
        data_loss_minutes = backup_age.total_seconds() / 60
        
        result = RecoveryTestResult(
            test_scenario="Full Database Recovery",
            start_time=start_time,
            end_time=end_time,
            recovery_time_seconds=recovery_time,
            data_loss_minutes=data_loss_minutes,
            success=success,
            verification_details=verification_details,
            errors=errors
        )
        
        self.results.append(result)
        return result
    
    def test_point_in_time_recovery(self, recovery_point: datetime) -> RecoveryTestResult:
        """Test recovery to specific timestamp"""
        print(f"🕒 Testing Point-in-Time Recovery to {recovery_point}...")
        start_time = datetime.now()
        errors = []
        
        try:
            # 1. Create test data before recovery point
            with self.prod_conn.cursor() as cur:
                cur.execute("""
                    INSERT INTO recovery_test_events 
                    (event_time, description) 
                    VALUES (%s, 'Before recovery point')
                """, (datetime.now(),))
                self.prod_conn.commit()
            
            # Wait to pass recovery point
            time.sleep(2)
            
            # 2. Create test data after recovery point
            with self.prod_conn.cursor() as cur:
                cur.execute("""
                    INSERT INTO recovery_test_events 
                    (event_time, description) 
                    VALUES (%s, 'After recovery point - should be lost')
                """, (datetime.now(),))
                self.prod_conn.commit()
            
            # 3. Perform point-in-time recovery
            test_db_name = f"pitr_test_{int(time.time())}"
            
            cmd = [
                'pg_restore',
                '--dbname', test_db_name,
                '--recovery-target-time', recovery_point.isoformat(),
                self.backup_location
            ]
            
            result = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True)
            
            if result.returncode != 0:
                errors.append(f"PITR failed: {result.stderr}")
            else:
                # 4. Verify only data before recovery point exists
                pitr_conn = psycopg2.connect(f"dbname={test_db_name}")
                with pitr_conn.cursor() as cur:
                    cur.execute("""
                        SELECT COUNT(*) as events_before,
                               MAX(event_time) as latest_event
                        FROM recovery_test_events
                        WHERE description LIKE '%Before%'
                    """)
                    before_data = cur.fetchone()
                    
                    cur.execute("""
                        SELECT COUNT(*) as events_after
                        FROM recovery_test_events
                        WHERE description LIKE '%After%'
                    """)
                    after_data = cur.fetchone()
                    
                    if after_data[0] > 0:
                        errors.append(f"Data beyond recovery point found: {after_data[0]} events")
                    
                    if before_data[0] == 0:
                        errors.append("No data before recovery point found")
                    
                    # Check latest event is <= recovery point
                    if before_data[1] and before_data[1] > recovery_point:
                        errors.append(f"Latest event {before_data[1]} is after recovery point {recovery_point}")
                
                pitr_conn.close()
            
            success = len(errors) == 0
            verification_details = f"Events before: {before_data[0] if 'before_data' in locals() else 'N/A'}, Events after: {after_data[0] if 'after_data' in locals() else 'N/A'}"
            
        except Exception as e:
            errors.append(str(e))
            success = False
            verification_details = f"Error: {e}"
        
        end_time = datetime.now()
        recovery_time = (end_time - start_time).total_seconds()
        
        result = RecoveryTestResult(
            test_scenario=f"Point-in-Time Recovery to {recovery_point}",
            start_time=start_time,
            end_time=end_time,
            recovery_time_seconds=recovery_time,
            data_loss_minutes=0,  # PITR should have minimal loss
            success=success,
            verification_details=verification_details,
            errors=errors
        )
        
        self.results.append(result)
        return result
    
    def test_partial_recovery(self, table_name: str) -> RecoveryTestResult:
        """Test recovery of single table"""
        print(f"🔧 Testing Partial Recovery: {table_name}...")
        start_time = datetime.now()
        errors = []
        
        try:
            # 1. Get table state before
            with self.prod_conn.cursor() as cur:
                cur.execute(f"SELECT COUNT(*) FROM {table_name}")
                original_count = cur.fetchone()[0]
            
            # 2. Simulate table corruption/deletion in test env
            test_db_name = f"partial_test_{int(time.time())}"
            
            # 3. Restore specific table
            cmd = [
                'pg_restore',
                '--dbname', test_db_name,
                '--table', table_name,
                self.backup_location
            ]
            
            result = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True)
            
            if result.returncode != 0:
                errors.append(f"Partial restore failed: {result.stderr}")
            else:
                # 4. Verify table restored
                test_conn = psycopg2.connect(f"dbname={test_db_name}")
                with test_conn.cursor() as cur:
                    cur.execute(f"SELECT COUNT(*) FROM {table_name}")
                    restored_count = cur.fetchone()[0]
                    
                    if restored_count != original_count:
                        errors.append(f"Count mismatch: Original {original_count}, Restored {restored_count}")
                
                test_conn.close()
            
            success = len(errors) == 0
            verification_details = f"Original: {original_count}, Restored: {restored_count if 'restored_count' in locals() else 'N/A'}"
            
        except Exception as e:
            errors.append(str(e))
            success = False
            verification_details = f"Error: {e}"
        
        end_time = datetime.now()
        recovery_time = (end_time - start_time).total_seconds()
        
        result = RecoveryTestResult(
            test_scenario=f"Partial Recovery: {table_name}",
            start_time=start_time,
            end_time=end_time,
            recovery_time_seconds=recovery_time,
            data_loss_minutes=0,
            success=success,
            verification_details=verification_details,
            errors=errors
        )
        
        self.results.append(result)
        return result
    
    def _capture_production_state(self) -> Dict:
        """Capture critical production metrics"""
        state = {}
        with self.prod_conn.cursor() as cur:
            # Table counts
            cur.execute("""
                SELECT tablename, COUNT(*) as row_count
                FROM (
                    SELECT 'users' as tablename FROM users UNION ALL
                    SELECT 'orders' FROM orders UNION ALL
                    SELECT 'products' FROM products
                ) t
                GROUP BY tablename
            """)
            state['table_counts'] = {row[0]: row[1] for row in cur.fetchall()}
            
            # Latest timestamps
            cur.execute("""
                SELECT 
                    MAX(created_at) as latest_user,
                    MAX(order_date) as latest_order,
                    MAX(updated_at) as latest_product
                FROM (
                    SELECT created_at, NULL as order_date, NULL as updated_at FROM users
                    UNION ALL
                    SELECT NULL, order_date, NULL FROM orders
                    UNION ALL
                    SELECT NULL, NULL, updated_at FROM products
                ) t
            """)
            state['latest_timestamps'] = cur.fetchone()
            
        return state
    
    def _verify_restored_data(self, test_db_name: str, original_state: Dict) -> Dict:
        """Verify restored data matches original"""
        test_conn = psycopg2.connect(f"dbname={test_db_name}")
        results = {"status": "pending", "details": {}}
        
        try:
            with test_conn.cursor() as cur:
                # Verify table counts
                for table, expected_count in original_state['table_counts'].items():
                    cur.execute(f"SELECT COUNT(*) FROM {table}")
                    actual_count = cur.fetchone()[0]
                    results['details'][f"{table}_count"] = {
                        "expected": expected_count,
                        "actual": actual_count,
                        "match": expected_count == actual_count
                    }
                
                # Verify latest data exists
                cur.execute("SELECT MAX(created_at) FROM users")
                latest_user = cur.fetchone()[0]
                results['details']["latest_user"] = {
                    "original": original_state['latest_timestamps'][0],
                    "restored": latest_user,
                    "match": original_state['latest_timestamps'][0] == latest_user
                }
                
            all_match = all(detail["match"] for detail in results['details'].values())
            results['status'] = "verified" if all_match else "mismatch"
            
        except Exception as e:
            results['status'] = f"error: {e}"
        finally:
            test_conn.close()
            
        return results
    
    def _test_application_functionality(self, test_db_name: str) -> Dict:
        """Test basic application functionality"""
        test_conn = psycopg2.connect(f"dbname={test_db_name}")
        results = {"success": False, "details": ""}
        
        try:
            with test_conn.cursor() as cur:
                # Test 1: Can query users
                cur.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM users WHERE status = 'active'")
                active_users = cur.fetchone()[0]
                
                # Test 2: Can join tables
                cur.execute("""
                    SELECT COUNT(*) 
                    FROM orders o
                    JOIN users u ON o.user_id = u.id
                    WHERE o.status = 'completed'
                """)
                completed_orders = cur.fetchone()[0]
                
                # Test 3: Basic business logic
                cur.execute("""
                    SELECT COUNT(*)
                    FROM products
                    WHERE price > 0 AND inventory_count >= 0
                """)
                valid_products = cur.fetchone()[0]
                
                results['success'] = True
                results['details'] = f"Active users: {active_users}, Completed orders: {completed_orders}, Valid products: {valid_products}"
                
        except Exception as e:
            results['details'] = f"Application test failed: {e}"
        finally:
            test_conn.close()
            
        return results
    
    def _get_backup_age(self) -> timedelta:
        """Get age of latest backup"""
        with self.prod_conn.cursor() as cur:
            cur.execute("SELECT MAX(backup_time) FROM backup_log WHERE success = true")
            latest_backup = cur.fetchone()[0]
            
            if latest_backup:
                return datetime.now() - latest_backup
            else:
                return timedelta(days=365)  # 1 year if no backups
    
    def generate_report(self):
        """Generate comprehensive test report"""
        print("\n" + "="*80)
        print("📊 RECOVERY TESTING REPORT")
        print("="*80)
        
        total_tests = len(self.results)
        successful_tests = sum(1 for r in self.results if r.success)
        failed_tests = total_tests - successful_tests
        
        # Overall statistics
        print(f"\nOverall Results: {successful_tests}/{total_tests} tests passed ({successful_tests/total_tests*100:.1f}%)")
        
        if failed_tests > 0:
            print(f"🚨 {failed_tests} tests FAILED - Immediate attention required!")
        
        # Detailed results
        print("\nDetailed Results:")
        print("-"*80)
        
        for result in self.results:
            status = "✅ PASS" if result.success else "❌ FAIL"
            print(f"\n{status} {result.test_scenario}")
            print(f"  Duration: {result.recovery_time_seconds:.1f} seconds")
            print(f"  Data Loss: {result.data_loss_minutes:.1f} minutes")
            print(f"  Verification: {result.verification_details}")
            
            if result.errors:
                print(f"  Errors:")
                for error in result.errors:
                    print(f"    • {error}")
        
        # RTO/RPO analysis
        print("\nRTO/RPO Analysis:")
        print("-"*80)
        
        rto_target = 240 * 60  # 4 hours in seconds
        rpo_target = 15  # 15 minutes
        
        rto_violations = [r for r in self.results if r.recovery_time_seconds > rto_target]
        rpo_violations = [r for r in self.results if r.data_loss_minutes > rpo_target]
        
        if rto_violations:
            print(f"🚨 RTO Violations: {len(rto_violations)} tests exceeded 4-hour recovery time")
            for violation in rto_violations:
                print(f"  • {violation.test_scenario}: {violation.recovery_time_seconds/60:.1f} minutes")
        else:
            print(f"✅ All tests met RTO (4-hour target)")
        
        if rpo_violations:
            print(f"\n🚨 RPO Violations: {len(rpo_violations)} tests exceeded 15-minute data loss")
            for violation in rpo_violations:
                print(f"  • {violation.test_scenario}: {violation.data_loss_minutes:.1f} minutes loss")
        else:
            print(f"✅ All tests met RPO (15-minute target)")
        
        # Recommendations
        print("\nRecommendations:")
        print("-"*80)
        
        if failed_tests > 0:
            print("1. IMMEDIATE ACTION REQUIRED:")
            print("   • Fix failed recovery tests before next backup cycle")
            print("   • Document root causes and remediation steps")
            print("   • Implement monitoring for identified failure points")
        
        # Analyze patterns
        slow_tests = [r for r in self.results if r.recovery_time_seconds > 300]  # >5 minutes
        high_loss_tests = [r for r in self.results if r.data_loss_minutes > 5]
        
        if slow_tests:
            print(f"\n2. Performance Improvements ({len(slow_tests)} slow tests):")
            avg_time = sum(r.recovery_time_seconds for r in slow_tests) / len(slow_tests)
            print(f"   • Average slow test time: {avg_time/60:.1f} minutes")
            print("   • Consider: Faster storage, parallel restore, backup optimization")
        
        if high_loss_tests:
            print(f"\n3. RPO Improvements ({len(high_loss_tests)} high-loss tests):")
            avg_loss = sum(r.data_loss_minutes for r in high_loss_tests) / len(high_loss_tests)
            print(f"   • Average data loss: {avg_loss:.1f} minutes")
            print("   • Consider: More frequent backups, transaction log shipping, replication")
        
        # Check testing coverage
        test_types = set(r.test_scenario for r in self.results)
        required_scenarios = {"Full Database Recovery", "Point-in-Time Recovery", "Partial Recovery"}
        missing_scenarios = required_scenarios - test_types
        
        if missing_scenarios:
            print(f"\n4. Coverage Gaps ({len(missing_scenarios)} missing scenarios):")
            for scenario in missing_scenarios:
                print(f"   • Missing test: {scenario}")
            print("   • Schedule missing tests within next 2 weeks")
        
        # Backup age warning
        oldest_backup = max(r.data_loss_minutes for r in self.results if r.data_loss_minutes > 0) if self.results else 0
        if oldest_backup > 1440:  # >24 hours
            print(f"\n5. Backup Frequency Issue:")
            print(f"   • Maximum data loss potential: {oldest_backup/60:.1f} hours")
            print("   • Increase backup frequency to meet RPO requirements")
        
        print("\n" + "="*80)
        print("Next Steps:")
        print("1. Review this report with recovery team")
        print("2. Create action items for identified issues")
        print("3. Update recovery documentation based on findings")
        print("4. Schedule next comprehensive test within 30 days")
        print("="*80)
        
        # Return summary
        return {
            "total_tests": total_tests,
            "successful_tests": successful_tests,
            "success_rate": successful_tests/total_tests*100 if total_tests > 0 else 0,
            "rto_violations": len(rto_violations),
            "rpo_violations": len(rpo_violations),
            "recommendations_count": sum([
                1 if failed_tests > 0 else 0,
                1 if slow_tests else 0,
                1 if high_loss_tests else 0,
                1 if missing_scenarios else 0,
                1 if oldest_backup > 1440 else 0
            ])
        }

def main():
    """Main execution function"""
    # Configuration
    PRODUCTION_DB = "host=localhost dbname=production user=admin password=secret"
    BACKUP_FILE = "/backups/latest_production.dump"
    
    # Initialize tester
    tester = RecoveryTester(PRODUCTION_DB, BACKUP_FILE)
    
    # Run comprehensive tests
    print("Starting Comprehensive Recovery Testing Suite")
    print("="*80)
    
    # Test 1: Full recovery
    result1 = tester.test_full_recovery()
    
    # Test 2: Point-in-time recovery (1 hour ago)
    recovery_point = datetime.now() - timedelta(hours=1)
    result2 = tester.test_point_in_time_recovery(recovery_point)
    
    # Test 3: Partial recovery of critical tables
    critical_tables = ["users", "orders", "products"]
    for table in critical_tables:
        result = tester.test_partial_recovery(table)
    
    # Generate report
    report = tester.generate_report()
    
    # Exit with appropriate code
    if report["success_rate"] < 90:
        print("\n🚨 CRITICAL: Recovery testing success rate below 90%")
        sys.exit(1)
    elif report["success_rate"] < 95:
        print("\n⚠️ WARNING: Recovery testing success rate below 95%")
        sys.exit(0)
    else:
        print("\n✅ SUCCESS: All recovery tests passed")
        sys.exit(0)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

content.caption: Automated Backup Health Dashboard
content.code:
-- Comprehensive backup health monitoring
CREATE TABLE backup_health_dashboard AS
WITH backup_metrics AS (
    SELECT 
        backup_id,
        backup_type,
        start_time,
        end_time,
        EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (end_time - start_time)) as duration_seconds,
        backup_size_gb,
        success,
        verification_status
    FROM backup_log
    WHERE backup_time > CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '30 days'
),
recovery_metrics AS (
    SELECT 
        test_id,
        test_scenario,
        recovery_start,
        recovery_end,
        EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (recovery_end - recovery_start)) as recovery_seconds,
        data_loss_minutes,
        success as recovery_success
    FROM recovery_tests
    WHERE test_date > CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '90 days'
),
sla_compliance AS (
    SELECT 
        'RTO Compliance' as metric,
        COUNT(*) as total_tests,
        SUM(CASE WHEN recovery_seconds <= 240 * 60 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as compliant_tests,  -- 4 hours
        ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN recovery_seconds <= 240 * 60 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(*), 2) as compliance_rate
    FROM recovery_metrics
    WHERE recovery_success = true
    UNION ALL
    SELECT 
        'RPO Compliance',
        COUNT(*),
        SUM(CASE WHEN data_loss_minutes <= 15 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END),  -- 15 minutes
        ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN data_loss_minutes <= 15 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(*), 2)
    FROM recovery_metrics
    WHERE recovery_success = true
)
SELECT 
    -- Backup success rate
    (SELECT 
        ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN success THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(*), 2)
     FROM backup_metrics) as backup_success_rate,
    
    -- Average backup duration
    (SELECT 
        ROUND(AVG(duration_seconds) / 60, 2)
     FROM backup_metrics 
     WHERE success = true) as avg_backup_minutes,
    
    -- Verification success rate
    (SELECT 
        ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN verification_status = 'verified' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(*), 2)
     FROM backup_metrics 
     WHERE success = true) as verification_rate,
    
    -- Recovery success rate
    (SELECT 
        ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN recovery_success THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(*), 2)
     FROM recovery_metrics) as recovery_success_rate,
    
    -- SLA compliance rates
    (SELECT compliance_rate FROM sla_compliance WHERE metric = 'RTO Compliance') as rto_compliance,
    (SELECT compliance_rate FROM sla_compliance WHERE metric = 'RPO Compliance') as rpo_compliance,
    
    -- Days since last full test
    (SELECT 
        EXTRACT(DAY FROM NOW() - MAX(test_date))
     FROM recovery_tests 
     WHERE test_scenario = 'Full Disaster Recovery') as days_since_full_test,
    
    -- Critical backup age
    (SELECT 
        EXTRACT(HOUR FROM NOW() - MAX(backup_time))
     FROM backup_log 
     WHERE backup_type = 'critical' 
       AND success = true) as hours_since_critical_backup;

-- Generate alerts
SELECT 
    CASE 
        WHEN backup_success_rate < 99 THEN '⚠️ Backup success rate below 99%'
        WHEN verification_rate < 95 THEN '⚠️ Verification rate below 95%'
        WHEN recovery_success_rate < 90 THEN '🚨 Recovery success rate below 90%'
        WHEN rto_compliance < 95 THEN '🚨 RTO compliance below 95%'
        WHEN rpo_compliance < 95 THEN '🚨 RPO compliance below 95%'
        WHEN days_since_full_test > 30 THEN '⚠️ Full recovery test overdue'
        WHEN hours_since_critical_backup > 24 THEN '⚠️ Critical backup overdue'
        ELSE '✅ All systems nominal'
    END as alert_status
FROM backup_health_dashboard;

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Chaos Engineering Recovery Testing
Inject failures during recovery to test resilience
"""

import random
import time
import threading
from datetime import datetime
from typing import Dict, List
import subprocess
import psutil
import socket

class ChaosInjector:
    """Inject controlled failures during recovery testing"""
    
    def __init__(self):
        self.active_injections = []
    
    def inject_network_latency(self, target_ip: str, latency_ms: int, duration_sec: int):
        """Add network latency to specific IP"""
        print(f"🌐 Injecting {latency_ms}ms latency to {target_ip} for {duration_sec}s")
        
        # Using tc (Linux traffic control)
        cmd = f"""
        sudo tc qdisc add dev eth0 root handle 1: prio
        sudo tc filter add dev eth0 parent 1:0 protocol ip prio 1 u32 \
          match ip dst {target_ip} flowid 1:1
        sudo tc qdisc add dev eth0 parent 1:1 handle 10: netem delay {latency_ms}ms
        """
        
        subprocess.run(cmd, shell=True, capture_output=True)
        
        # Schedule removal
        def remove_latency():
            time.sleep(duration_sec)
            subprocess.run("sudo tc qdisc del dev eth0 root", shell=True)
            print(f"✅ Removed latency injection for {target_ip}")
        
        thread = threading.Thread(target=remove_latency)
        thread.start()
        self.active_injections.append(thread)
    
    def inject_packet_loss(self, loss_percent: int, duration_sec: int):
        """Inject packet loss"""
        print(f"📦 Injecting {loss_percent}% packet loss for {duration_sec}s")
        
        cmd = f"""
        sudo tc qdisc add dev eth0 root netem loss {loss_percent}%
        """
        
        subprocess.run(cmd, shell=True)
        
        def remove_loss():
            time.sleep(duration_sec)
            subprocess.run("sudo tc qdisc del dev eth0 root", shell=True)
            print("✅ Removed packet loss injection")
        
        thread = threading.Thread(target=remove_loss)
        thread.start()
        self.active_injections.append(thread)
    
    def limit_bandwidth(self, bandwidth_mbps: int, duration_sec: int):
        """Limit network bandwidth"""
        print(f"🚦 Limiting bandwidth to {bandwidth_mbps}Mbps for {duration_sec}s")
        
        cmd = f"""
        sudo tc qdisc add dev eth0 root tbf rate {bandwidth_mbps}mbit \
          burst 100kb latency 50ms
        """
        
        subprocess.run(cmd, shell=True)
        
        def remove_limit():
            time.sleep(duration_sec)
            subprocess.run("sudo tc qdisc del dev eth0 root", shell=True)
            print("✅ Removed bandwidth limitation")
        
        thread = threading.Thread(target=remove_limit)
        thread.start()
        self.active_injections.append(thread)
    
    def stress_cpu(self, cpu_percent: int, duration_sec: int):
        """Stress CPU to simulate high load"""
        print(f"🔥 Stressing CPU to {cpu_percent}% for {duration_sec}s")
        
        def cpu_stressor():
            end_time = time.time() + duration_sec
            while time.time() < end_time:
                # Calculate primes to consume CPU
                for i in range(2, 10000):
                    all(i % j != 0 for j in range(2, int(i**0.5) + 1))
                time.sleep(0.01)  # Small sleep to allow other threads
            print("✅ CPU stress test completed")
        
        # Start multiple threads to reach target CPU%
        num_threads = psutil.cpu_count() * cpu_percent // 100
        for _ in range(num_threads):
            thread = threading.Thread(target=cpu_stressor)
            thread.start()
            self.active_injections.append(thread)
    
    def fill_disk(self, target_path: str, fill_percent: int):
        """Fill disk to simulate low disk space"""
        print(f"💾 Filling disk at {target_path} to {fill_percent}% capacity")
        
        # Get current disk usage
        disk_usage = psutil.disk_usage(target_path)
        free_bytes = disk_usage.free
        target_free = disk_usage.total * (100 - fill_percent) / 100
        bytes_to_fill = free_bytes - target_free
        
        if bytes_to_fill > 0:
            # Create a file to fill the space
            fill_file = f"{target_path}/chaos_fill.bin"
            chunk_size = 1024 * 1024  # 1MB chunks
            
            with open(fill_file, 'wb') as f:
                bytes_written = 0
                while bytes_written < bytes_to_fill:
                    chunk = b'0' * min(chunk_size, bytes_to_fill - bytes_written)
                    f.write(chunk)
                    bytes_written += len(chunk)
                    
                    # Check if we've reached target
                    current_usage = psutil.disk_usage(target_path)
                    if current_usage.percent >= fill_percent:
                        break
            
            print(f"✅ Disk filled to {psutil.disk_usage(target_path).percent}%")
            return fill_file
        return None
    
    def simulate_process_failure(self, process_name: str, kill_method: str = "SIGTERM"):
        """Simulate process failure during recovery"""
        print(f"💀 Killing process {process_name} with {kill_method}")
        
        for proc in psutil.process_iter(['pid', 'name']):
            if process_name in proc.info['name']:
                try:
                    if kill_method == "SIGKILL":
                        proc.kill()
                    else:
                        proc.terminate()
                    print(f"✅ Killed process {proc.info['name']} (PID: {proc.info['pid']})")
                    return True
                except psutil.NoSuchProcess:
                    pass
        return False
    
    def wait_for_completion(self, timeout_sec: int = 300):
        """Wait for all chaos injections to complete"""
        print(f"⏳ Waiting for chaos injections to complete (timeout: {timeout_sec}s)")
        
        start_time = time.time()
        for thread in self.active_injections:
            remaining = timeout_sec - (time.time() - start_time)
            if remaining > 0:
                thread.join(timeout=remaining)
        
        print("✅ All chaos injections completed")
    
    def cleanup(self):
        """Clean up any remaining chaos injections"""
        print("🧹 Cleaning up chaos injections")
        
        # Remove any tc rules
        subprocess.run("sudo tc qdisc del dev eth0 root 2>/dev/null || true", shell=True)
        
        # Clean up disk fill files
        subprocess.run("find /tmp -name 'chaos_fill.bin' -delete 2>/dev/null || true", shell=True)
        
        print("✅ Chaos cleanup complete")

class ChaosRecoveryTester:
    """Recovery testing with chaos engineering"""
    
    def __init__(self, recovery_tester, chaos_injector):
        self.recovery_tester = recovery_tester
        self.chaos = chaos_injector
        
    def test_recovery_under_load(self):
        """Test recovery while system is under high load"""
        print("\n🧪 Testing Recovery Under Load")
        print("="*60)
        
        # 1. Start CPU stress
        self.chaos.stress_cpu(80, 300)  # 80% CPU for 5 minutes
        
        # 2. Limit bandwidth
        self.chaos.limit_bandwidth(10, 300)  # 10Mbps limit
        
        # 3. Test recovery
        result = self.recovery_tester.test_full_recovery()
        
        # 4. Wait for chaos to complete
        self.chaos.wait_for_completion()
        
        return result
    
    def test_recovery_with_network_issues(self):
        """Test recovery with network problems"""
        print("\n🧪 Testing Recovery with Network Issues")
        print("="*60)
        
        # 1. Add latency to backup server
        backup_server_ip = "192.168.1.100"  # Example IP
        self.chaos.inject_network_latency(backup_server_ip, 500, 300)  # 500ms latency
        
        # 2. Add packet loss
        self.chaos.inject_packet_loss(5, 300)  # 5% packet loss
        
        # 3. Test recovery
        result = self.recovery_tester.test_full_recovery()
        
        self.chaos.wait_for_completion()
        return result
    
    def test_recovery_with_disk_pressure(self, target_path: str = "/tmp"):
        """Test recovery with low disk space"""
        print("\n🧪 Testing Recovery with Disk Pressure")
        print("="*60)
        
        # 1. Fill disk to 90%
        fill_file = self.chaos.fill_disk(target_path, 90)
        
        # 2. Test recovery (should handle disk space issues)
        result = self.recovery_tester.test_full_recovery()
        
        # 3. Clean up fill file
        if fill_file:
            import os
            os.remove(fill_file)
            
        return result
    
    def test_recovery_with_process_failures(self):
        """Test recovery when critical processes fail"""
        print("\n🧪 Testing Recovery with Process Failures")
        print("="*60)
        
        # 1. Kill database process mid-recovery
        print("Starting recovery, will kill process at 30% completion...")
        
        # Start recovery in background
        recovery_thread = threading.Thread(
            target=self.recovery_tester.test_full_recovery
        )
        recovery_thread.start()
        
        # Wait a bit, then kill process
        time.sleep(15)  # Wait for recovery to be partially done
        
        print("Injecting process failure...")
        self.chaos.simulate_process_failure("postgres", "SIGKILL")
        
        # Wait for recovery to finish (should fail or restart)
        recovery_thread.join(timeout=300)
        
        # Note: This test expects failure - we're testing if recovery
        # procedures handle process crashes properly
        print("✅ Process failure injection complete")
        
        return {
            "test_scenario": "Recovery with Process Failures",
            "success": False,  # Expected to fail
            "details": "Test verifies recovery procedures handle process crashes"
        }
    
    def run_comprehensive_chaos_test(self):
        """Run all chaos tests and generate report"""
        print("\n🌀 Starting Comprehensive Chaos Recovery Testing")
        print("="*80)
        
        results = []
        
        # Run each chaos scenario
        chaos_scenarios = [
            ("Recovery Under Load", self.test_recovery_under_load),
            ("Network Issues", self.test_recovery_with_network_issues),
            ("Disk Pressure", lambda: self.test_recovery_with_disk_pressure()),
            ("Process Failures", self.test_recovery_with_process_failures)
        ]
        
        for scenario_name, test_func in chaos_scenarios:
            print(f"\n📋 Scenario: {scenario_name}")
            print("-"*40)
            
            try:
                result = test_func()
                if isinstance(result, dict):
                    results.append({"scenario": scenario_name, **result})
                else:
                    results.append({
                        "scenario": scenario_name,
                        "success": result.success,
                        "details": result.verification_details,
                        "errors": result.errors
                    })
            except Exception as e:
                print(f"❌ Test failed with exception: {e}")
                results.append({
                    "scenario": scenario_name,
                    "success": False,
                    "details": f"Exception: {str(e)}",
                    "errors": [str(e)]
                })
            
            # Brief pause between scenarios
            time.sleep(5)
        
        # Generate chaos test report
        self._generate_chaos_report(results)
        
        return results
    
    def _generate_chaos_report(self, results):
        """Generate detailed chaos testing report"""
        print("\n" + "="*80)
        print("🌀 CHAOS RECOVERY TESTING REPORT")
        print("="*80)
        
        total_tests = len(results)
        successful_tests = sum(1 for r in results if r.get("success", False))
        
        print(f"\nOverall Results: {successful_tests}/{total_tests} scenarios handled")
        
        # Resilience scoring
        resilience_score = 0
        max_score = total_tests * 10
        
        print("\nResilience Analysis:")
        print("-"*80)
        
        for result in results:
            scenario = result["scenario"]
            success = result.get("success", False)
            
            # Score based on scenario complexity
            if "Load" in scenario:
                weight = 10
            elif "Network" in scenario:
                weight = 8
            elif "Disk" in scenario:
                weight = 7
            elif "Process" in scenario:
                weight = 9  # Process failures are critical
            else:
                weight = 5
            
            if success:
                resilience_score += weight
                print(f"✅ {scenario}: +{weight} points (Handled)")
            else:
                # Check if failure was expected
                if "Expected to fail" in str(result.get("details", "")):
                    resilience_score += weight // 2  # Partial credit for testing failure
                    print(f"⚠️  {scenario}: +{weight//2} points (Tested failure case)")
                else:
                    print(f"❌ {scenario}: 0 points (Failed unexpectedly)")
        
        # Calculate resilience percentage
        resilience_pct = (resilience_score / max_score) * 100 if max_score > 0 else 0
        
        print(f"\n📊 Resilience Score: {resilience_score}/{max_score} ({resilience_pct:.1f}%)")
        
        # Recommendations
        print("\n🔧 Recommendations:")
        print("-"*80)
        
        if resilience_pct >= 90:
            print("✅ Excellent resilience! Maintain current testing practices.")
        elif resilience_pct >= 70:
            print("⚠️  Good resilience. Consider:")
            print("   • Adding more chaos scenarios")
            print("   • Testing with combined failures")
            print("   • Increasing frequency of chaos tests")
        else:
            print("🚨 Critical resilience gaps identified:")
            
            failed_scenarios = [r["scenario"] for r in results 
                              if not r.get("success", False) 
                              and "Expected" not in str(r.get("details", ""))]
            
            if failed_scenarios:
                print("   • Immediate fixes needed for:")
                for scenario in failed_scenarios:
                    print(f"     - {scenario}")
            
            print("   • Implement retry logic in recovery scripts")
            print("   • Add circuit breakers for external dependencies")
            print("   • Create degraded mode operation plans")
        
        # Specific improvements based on failures
        for result in results:
            if not result.get("success", False) and "Expected" not in str(result.get("details", "")):
                scenario = result["scenario"]
                errors = result.get("errors", [])
                
                print(f"\n   Specific improvements for {scenario}:")
                for error in errors[:3]:  # Top 3 errors
                    if "timeout" in error.lower():
                        print(f"     • Increase timeouts or implement exponential backoff")
                    elif "disk" in error.lower() or "space" in error.lower():
                        print(f"     • Add disk space checks before recovery")
                        print(f"     • Implement automatic cleanup of temp files")
                    elif "connection" in error.lower() or "network" in error.lower():
                        print(f"     • Add network resilience with retries")
                        print(f"     • Implement fallback to local cache")
        
        print("\n" + "="*80)
        print("Next Chaos Testing Steps:")
        print("1. Review findings with reliability engineering team")
        print("2. Update recovery documentation with chaos learnings")
        print("3. Schedule regular chaos recovery tests (quarterly)")
        print("4. Expand chaos scenarios based on business criticality")
        print("="*80)

# Example usage
if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Initialize components
    from recovery_tester import RecoveryTester  # Assuming previous module
    
    recovery_tester = RecoveryTester(
        production_conn_str="host=localhost dbname=test",
        backup_location="/backups/test.dump"
    )
    
    chaos_injector = ChaosInjector()
    chaos_tester = ChaosRecoveryTester(recovery_tester, chaos_injector)
    
    try:
        # Run comprehensive chaos testing
        results = chaos_tester.run_comprehensive_chaos_test()
        
        # Cleanup
        chaos_injector.cleanup()
        
        # Exit based on results
        successful_scenarios = sum(1 for r in results if r.get("success", False))
        total_scenarios = len(results)
        
        if successful_scenarios / total_scenarios >= 0.7:
            print("\n✅ Chaos testing completed with acceptable resilience")
            exit(0)
        else:
            print("\n🚨 Chaos testing revealed critical resilience gaps")
            exit(1)
            
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        print("\n⚠️ Chaos testing interrupted by user")
        chaos_injector.cleanup()
        exit(130)
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"\n❌ Chaos testing failed: {e}")
        chaos_injector.cleanup()
        exit(1)

content.title: Game Day Exercises: Turning Testing into Training
content.explanation: Game Days are live, time-boxed exercises where teams simulate disasters and execute recovery procedures. Benefits: 1) Validate recovery procedures under pressure, 2) Train teams on actual recovery processes, 3) Identify knowledge gaps and procedure flaws, 4) Build muscle memory for real disasters. Structure: 1) Planning (scenarios, objectives), 2) Briefing (rules, safety), 3) Execution (inject failures, observe), 4) Debrief (lessons learned, improvements).

content.code:
#!/bin/bash

# Kubernetes Stateful Application Recovery Testing
# Tests recovery of stateful applications with persistent data

set -e

echo "🧪 Starting Kubernetes Stateful Application Recovery Test"
echo "====================================================="

# Configuration
NAMESPACE="recovery-test-$(date +%s)"
BACKUP_LOCATION="s3://backups/production/k8s/$(date +%Y-%m-%d)"
RESTORE_LOCATION="s3://backups/production/k8s/latest"

# Create test namespace
kubectl create namespace "$NAMESPACE"
echo "✅ Created namespace: $NAMESPACE"

# Function to simulate disaster
simulate_disaster() {
    echo "\n🔥 Simulating disaster scenario"
    echo "------------------------------"
    
    # Scale down stateful application
    kubectl -n "$NAMESPACE" scale deployment my-stateful-app --replicas=0
    echo "• Scaled down application to 0 replicas"
    
    # Delete persistent volume claims (simulating data loss)
    kubectl -n "$NAMESPACE" delete pvc --all --wait=false
    echo "• Deleted PersistentVolumeClaims (simulating storage failure)"
    
    # Delete configuration
    kubectl -n "$NAMESPACE" delete configmap app-config --wait=false
    echo "• Deleted configuration"
    
    # Wait for resources to be deleted
    sleep 30
    echo "✅ Disaster simulation complete"
}

# Function to backup current state
backup_state() {
    echo "\n💾 Backing up current state"
    echo "-------------------------"
    
    # Backup namespace resources
    kubectl -n "$NAMESPACE" get all -o yaml > "$NAMESPACE-backup.yaml"
    echo "• Backed up all resources to $NAMESPACE-backup.yaml"
    
    # Backup PVCs using velero (if installed)
    if command -v velero &> /dev/null; then
        velero backup create "$NAMESPACE-backup" --include-namespaces "$NAMESPACE" --wait
        echo "• Created Velero backup: $NAMESPACE-backup"
    fi
    
    # Backup etcd data for stateful applications
    kubectl -n "$NAMESPACE" get pvc -o json | jq -r '.items[].spec.volumeName' | while read volume; do
        if [ -n "$volume" ]; then
            echo "• Volume to backup: $volume"
            # Here you would implement actual volume backup
            # This could be cloud provider snapshots or storage system backups
        fi
    done
    
    echo "✅ State backup complete"
}

# Function to restore from backup
restore_state() {
    echo "\n🔧 Restoring from backup"
    echo "----------------------"
    
    local start_time=$(date +%s)
    
    # Restore namespace
    kubectl apply -f "$NAMESPACE-backup.yaml"
    echo "• Restored namespace resources"
    
    # Restore PVCs using velero
    if command -v velero &> /dev/null; then
        velero restore create --from-backup "$NAMESPACE-backup" --wait
        echo "• Restored from Velero backup"
    fi
    
    # Wait for volumes to be provisioned
    echo "• Waiting for PersistentVolumeClaims to be bound"
    kubectl -n "$NAMESPACE" wait --for=condition=bound pvc --all --timeout=300s
    
    # Scale up application
    kubectl -n "$NAMESPACE" scale deployment my-stateful-app --replicas=3
    echo "• Scaled application to 3 replicas"
    
    # Wait for pods to be ready
    echo "• Waiting for pods to be ready"
    kubectl -n "$NAMESPACE" wait --for=condition=ready pod -l app=my-stateful-app --timeout=300s
    
    local end_time=$(date +%s)
    local duration=$((end_time - start_time))
    
    echo "✅ Restore completed in $duration seconds"
    
    return $duration
}

# Function to validate recovery
validate_recovery() {
    echo "\n✅ Validating recovery"
    echo "-------------------"
    
    local success=true
    
    # Check all pods are running
    local running_pods=$(kubectl -n "$NAMESPACE" get pods -l app=my-stateful-app --field-selector=status.phase=Running | wc -l)
    if [ "$running_pods" -lt 3 ]; then
        echo "❌ Not all pods are running (found $running_pods/3)"
        success=false
    else
        echo "• All 3 application pods are running"
    fi
    
    # Check PVCs are bound
    local bound_pvcs=$(kubectl -n "$NAMESPACE" get pvc --no-headers | grep -c Bound)
    local total_pvcs=$(kubectl -n "$NAMESPACE" get pvc --no-headers | wc -l)
    
    if [ "$bound_pvcs" -ne "$total_pvcs" ]; then
        echo "❌ Not all PVCs are bound ($bound_pvcs/$total_pvcs)"
        success=false
    else
        echo "• All PVCs are bound"
    fi
    
    # Test application connectivity
    local service_name="my-stateful-app-service"
    local test_pod="recovery-test-$(date +%s)"
    
    # Create test pod
    kubectl -n "$NAMESPACE" run "$test_pod" --image=curlimages/curl -- sleep 3600
    kubectl -n "$NAMESPACE" wait --for=condition=ready pod "$test_pod" --timeout=60s
    
    # Test connectivity
    if kubectl -n "$NAMESPACE" exec "$test_pod" -- curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" "http://$service_name:8080/health" | grep -q "200"; then
        echo "• Application health check passed"
    else
        echo "❌ Application health check failed"
        success=false
    fi
    
    # Test data persistence
    if kubectl -n "$NAMESPACE" exec "$test_pod" -- curl -s "http://$service_name:8080/api/data" | grep -q "expected_data_pattern"; then
        echo "• Data persistence verified"
    else
        echo "⚠️  Data pattern not found (may be expected for clean restore)"
    fi
    
    # Clean up test pod
    kubectl -n "$NAMESPACE" delete pod "$test_pod" --wait=false
    
    if [ "$success" = true ]; then
        echo "✅ Recovery validation successful"
        return 0
    else
        echo "❌ Recovery validation failed"
        return 1
    fi
}

# Function to test cross-region recovery
test_cross_region_recovery() {
    echo "\n🌍 Testing Cross-Region Recovery"
    echo "-------------------------------"
    
    # Switch kubectl context to DR region
    local original_context=$(kubectl config current-context)
    kubectl config use-context dr-region
    
    echo "• Switched to DR region context"
    
    # Create namespace in DR region
    kubectl create namespace "$NAMESPACE-dr" || true
    
    # Deploy application from backup in DR region
    echo "• Deploying application in DR region"
    kubectl -n "$NAMESPACE-dr" apply -f "$NAMESPACE-backup.yaml"
    
    # Modify for DR region (different storage classes, etc.)
    kubectl -n "$NAMESPACE-dr" patch pvc my-data-pvc -p '
    {
        "spec": {
            "storageClassName": "dr-region-storage"
        }
    }'
    
    # Wait for deployment
    kubectl -n "$NAMESPACE-dr" wait --for=condition=available deployment/my-stateful-app --timeout=300s
    
    # Validate in DR region
    validate_recovery
    
    # Switch back to original context
    kubectl config use-context "$original_context"
    
    echo "✅ Cross-region recovery test complete"
}

# Function to test incremental recovery
test_incremental_recovery() {
    echo "\n🔄 Testing Incremental Recovery"
    echo "------------------------------"
    
    # Simulate ongoing operations
    echo "• Simulating ongoing data operations"
    
    # Create test data
    local test_pod="incremental-test-$(date +%s)"
    kubectl -n "$NAMESPACE" run "$test_pod" --image=curlimages/curl -- sleep 3600
    kubectl -n "$NAMESPACE" wait --for=condition=ready pod "$test_pod" --timeout=60s
    
    # Add initial data
    kubectl -n "$NAMESPACE" exec "$test_pod" -- curl -X POST "http://my-stateful-app-service:8080/api/data" -d '{"id":1,"value":"initial"}'
    
    # Take incremental backup
    echo "• Taking incremental backup"
    if command -v velero &> /dev/null; then
        velero backup create "$NAMESPACE-incremental" --include-namespaces "$NAMESPACE" --wait --snapshot-volumes
    fi
    
    # Add more data
    kubectl -n "$NAMESPACE" exec "$test_pod" -- curl -X POST "http://my-stateful-app-service:8080/api/data" -d '{"id":2,"value":"incremental"}'
    
    # Simulate corruption of new data
    echo "• Simulating data corruption"
    kubectl -n "$NAMESPACE" delete pod -l app=my-stateful-app --wait=false
    
    # Restore from incremental backup
    echo "• Restoring from incremental backup"
    if command -v velero &> /dev/null; then
        velero restore create --from-backup "$NAMESPACE-incremental" --wait
    fi
    
    # Verify initial data exists but incremental may be lost
    echo "• Verifying data state"
    local data_check=$(kubectl -n "$NAMESPACE" exec "$test_pod" -- curl -s "http://my-stateful-app-service:8080/api/data/1")
    
    if echo "$data_check" | grep -q "initial"; then
        echo "✅ Initial data preserved"
    else
        echo "❌ Initial data lost"
    fi
    
    # Clean up
    kubectl -n "$NAMESPACE" delete pod "$test_pod" --wait=false
    
    echo "✅ Incremental recovery test complete"
}

# Main execution
main() {
    echo "\n📋 Test Plan"
    echo "-----------"
    echo "1. Backup current state"
    echo "2. Simulate disaster"
    echo "3. Restore from backup"
    echo "4. Validate recovery"
    echo "5. Test cross-region recovery (optional)"
    echo "6. Test incremental recovery (optional)"
    
    # Step 1: Backup
    backup_state
    
    # Step 2: Simulate disaster
    simulate_disaster
    
    # Step 3: Restore
    restore_state
    restore_duration=$?
    
    # Step 4: Validate
    if validate_recovery; then
        echo "\n🎉 Recovery test successful!"
        echo "• Restore duration: $restore_duration seconds"
        
        # Record RTO compliance
        if [ "$restore_duration" -le 240 ]; then  # 4 hour RTO
            echo "• ✅ RTO achieved: Within 4 hours"
        else
            echo "• ⚠️  RTO missed: $((restore_duration/60)) minutes"
        fi
    else
        echo "\n❌ Recovery test failed"
        exit 1
    fi
    
    # Optional: Cross-region test
    if [ "${ENABLE_CROSS_REGION_TEST:-false}" = "true" ]; then
        test_cross_region_recovery
    fi
    
    # Optional: Incremental recovery test
    if [ "${ENABLE_INCREMENTAL_TEST:-false}" = "true" ]; then
        test_incremental_recovery
    fi
    
    # Cleanup
    echo "\n🧹 Cleaning up test resources"
    kubectl delete namespace "$NAMESPACE" --wait=false
    if [ "${ENABLE_CROSS_REGION_TEST:-false}" = "true" ]; then
        kubectl --context=dr-region delete namespace "$NAMESPACE-dr" --wait=false
    fi
    
    echo "\n✅ All tests completed successfully!"
}

# Run main function
main "$@"

content.title: Recovery Testing for Databases: Beyond Simple Backups
content.explanation: Database recovery requires specialized testing: 1) Test recovery with transaction log replay, 2) Validate consistency after restore (DBCC CHECKDB), 3) Test recovery with in-flight transactions, 4) Validate replication recovery (log shipping, mirroring), 5) Test recovery with large objects (BLOBs, geospatial data), 6) Validate recovery with encrypted databases, 7) Test recovery with compressed backups.

content.caption: Comprehensive Database Recovery Validation Queries
content.code:
-- Comprehensive Database Recovery Validation
-- Run these after recovery to ensure database integrity

-- 1. Basic Integrity Checks
PRINT '1. Basic Database Integrity';
GO

-- Check database state
SELECT 
    name,
    state_desc,
    recovery_model_desc,
    log_reuse_wait_desc,
    is_auto_close_on,
    is_auto_shrink_on
FROM sys.databases 
WHERE name = DB_NAME();
GO

-- 2. Schema Validation
PRINT '\n2. Schema Validation';
GO

-- Check for missing tables from critical list
DECLARE @ExpectedTables TABLE (TableName VARCHAR(255));
INSERT INTO @ExpectedTables VALUES 
    ('users'), ('orders'), ('products'), ('payments'), 
    ('inventory'), ('customers'), ('transactions');

SELECT 
    'Missing Table' as IssueType,
    et.TableName
FROM @ExpectedTables et
WHERE NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 
    FROM sys.tables t 
    WHERE t.name = et.TableName
)
UNION ALL
-- Check for tables with 0 rows
SELECT 
    'Empty Critical Table' as IssueType,
    t.name as TableName
FROM sys.tables t
JOIN @ExpectedTables et ON t.name = et.TableName
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM t);
GO

-- 3. Data Consistency Checks
PRINT '\n3. Data Consistency Checks';
GO

-- Foreign Key Integrity
SELECT 
    'Broken Foreign Key' as IssueType,
    OBJECT_NAME(fk.parent_object_id) as ChildTable,
    OBJECT_NAME(fk.referenced_object_id) as ParentTable,
    fk.name as ForeignKeyName,
    COUNT(*) as ViolationCount
FROM sys.foreign_keys fk
CROSS APPLY (
    SELECT COUNT(*) as cnt
    FROM (
        SELECT * 
        FROM fk.parent_object_id
        WHERE NOT EXISTS (
            SELECT 1 
            FROM fk.referenced_object_id r
            WHERE r.primary_key = fk.parent_object_id.foreign_key
        )
    ) v
) violations
WHERE violations.cnt > 0
GROUP BY fk.parent_object_id, fk.referenced_object_id, fk.name;
GO

-- Check Identity Gaps (may indicate data loss)
SELECT 
    'Large Identity Gap' as IssueType,
    OBJECT_NAME(object_id) as TableName,
    last_value as LastIdentity,
    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM OBJECT_NAME(object_id)) as RowCount,
    CAST((last_value - (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM OBJECT_NAME(object_id))) * 100.0 / last_value AS DECIMAL(5,2)) as GapPercent
FROM sys.identity_columns 
WHERE last_value > 1000  -- Only check tables with significant data
  AND (last_value - (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM OBJECT_NAME(object_id))) * 100.0 / last_value > 10;  -- More than 10% gap
GO

-- 4. Business Logic Validation
PRINT '\n4. Business Logic Validation';
GO

-- Check for invalid data states
SELECT 
    'Business Rule Violation' as IssueType,
    'Negative Price' as Rule,
    COUNT(*) as ViolationCount
FROM products 
WHERE price < 0
UNION ALL
SELECT 
    'Business Rule Violation',
    'Future Order Date',
    COUNT(*)
FROM orders 
WHERE order_date > GETDATE()
UNION ALL
SELECT 
    'Business Rule Violation',
    'Negative Inventory',
    COUNT(*)
FROM inventory 
WHERE quantity < 0;
GO

-- 5. Index Integrity
PRINT '\n5. Index Integrity';
GO

-- Check for corrupt indexes
SELECT 
    'Index Corruption' as IssueType,
    OBJECT_NAME(i.object_id) as TableName,
    i.name as IndexName,
    ips.avg_fragmentation_in_percent,
    ips.page_count
FROM sys.dm_db_index_physical_stats(DB_ID(), NULL, NULL, NULL, 'DETAILED') ips
JOIN sys.indexes i ON ips.object_id = i.object_id AND ips.index_id = i.index_id
WHERE ips.avg_fragmentation_in_percent > 30  -- High fragmentation
   OR ips.page_count = 0  -- Empty index
   OR ips.ghost_record_count > 1000;  -- Many ghost records
GO

-- 6. Temporal Data Validation
PRINT '\n6. Temporal Data Validation';
GO

-- Check temporal tables consistency
IF EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM sys.tables WHERE temporal_type = 2)  -- History table
BEGIN
    SELECT 
        'Temporal Data Issue' as IssueType,
        OBJECT_NAME(t.object_id) as TemporalTable,
        MIN(h.ValidFrom) as EarliestHistory,
        MAX(h.ValidTo) as LatestHistory,
        COUNT(*) as HistoryRows,
        (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM t) as CurrentRows
    FROM sys.tables t
    JOIN sys.tables h ON t.history_table_id = h.object_id
    WHERE t.temporal_type = 2
    GROUP BY t.object_id, h.object_id
    HAVING COUNT(*) = 0 OR (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM t) = 0;
END
GO

-- 7. Recovery Point Validation
PRINT '\n7. Recovery Point Validation';
GO

-- Check if recovery point is within RPO
DECLARE @RPO_MINUTES INT = 15;  -- 15 minute RPO
DECLARE @LastBackupTime DATETIME;
DECLARE @LastTransactionTime DATETIME;

-- Get last backup time
SELECT TOP 1 @LastBackupTime = backup_finish_date
FROM msdb.dbo.backupset 
WHERE database_name = DB_NAME() 
  AND type = 'D'  -- Full backup
ORDER BY backup_finish_date DESC;

-- Get last transaction time
SELECT @LastTransactionTime = MAX(last_transaction_time)
FROM (
    SELECT MAX(modified_date) as last_transaction_time FROM users
    UNION ALL
    SELECT MAX(order_date) FROM orders
    UNION ALL
    SELECT MAX(transaction_date) FROM transactions
) all_transactions;

SELECT 
    'RPO Compliance' as CheckType,
    @LastBackupTime as LastBackup,
    @LastTransactionTime as LastTransaction,
    DATEDIFF(MINUTE, @LastBackupTime, @LastTransactionTime) as DataLossMinutes,
    CASE 
        WHEN DATEDIFF(MINUTE, @LastBackupTime, @LastTransactionTime) <= @RPO_MINUTES
        THEN '✅ Within RPO'
        ELSE CONCAT('❌ RPO Violation: ', 
                   DATEDIFF(MINUTE, @LastBackupTime, @LastTransactionTime), 
                   ' minutes loss')
    END as Status;
GO

-- 8. Performance Baseline Check
PRINT '\n8. Performance Baseline Check';
GO

-- Compare performance metrics with baseline
WITH CurrentStats AS (
    SELECT 
        OBJECT_NAME(s.object_id) as TableName,
        s.row_count,
        s.reserved_page_count * 8 / 1024 as SizeMB
    FROM sys.dm_db_partition_stats s
    WHERE OBJECT_NAME(s.object_id) IN ('users', 'orders', 'products')
),
BaselineStats AS (
    -- This would come from a baseline table
    SELECT 
        TableName,
        row_count as baseline_rows,
        SizeMB as baseline_size
    FROM recovery_baseline
    WHERE check_date = DATEADD(DAY, -1, CAST(GETDATE() AS DATE))
)
SELECT 
    'Performance Deviation' as IssueType,
    cs.TableName,
    cs.row_count as CurrentRows,
    bs.baseline_rows as BaselineRows,
    cs.SizeMB as CurrentSize,
    bs.baseline_size as BaselineSize,
    CASE 
        WHEN ABS(cs.row_count - bs.baseline_rows) * 100.0 / NULLIF(bs.baseline_rows, 0) > 10
        THEN CONCAT('Row count deviation: ', 
                   CAST(ABS(cs.row_count - bs.baseline_rows) * 100.0 / NULLIF(bs.baseline_rows, 0) AS VARCHAR(10)), '%')
        WHEN ABS(cs.SizeMB - bs.baseline_size) * 100.0 / NULLIF(bs.baseline_size, 0) > 20
        THEN CONCAT('Size deviation: ', 
                   CAST(ABS(cs.SizeMB - bs.baseline_size) * 100.0 / NULLIF(bs.baseline_size, 0) AS VARCHAR(10)), '%')
        ELSE NULL
    END as Deviation
FROM CurrentStats cs
LEFT JOIN BaselineStats bs ON cs.TableName = bs.TableName
WHERE bs.TableName IS NOT NULL
  AND (
    ABS(cs.row_count - bs.baseline_rows) * 100.0 / NULLIF(bs.baseline_rows, 0) > 10
    OR ABS(cs.SizeMB - bs.baseline_size) * 100.0 / NULLIF(bs.baseline_size, 0) > 20
  );
GO

-- 9. Security Validation
PRINT '\n9. Security Validation';
GO

-- Check critical permissions are restored
SELECT 
    'Missing Permission' as IssueType,
    dp.name as PrincipalName,
    OBJECT_NAME(major_id) as ObjectName,
    permission_name
FROM sys.database_permissions p
JOIN sys.database_principals dp ON p.grantee_principal_id = dp.principal_id
WHERE dp.name IN (
    'app_user', 'report_user', 'admin_user'  -- Critical application roles
)
  AND state_desc = 'GRANT'
  AND NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 
    FROM restored_permissions_baseline b
    WHERE b.principal_name = dp.name
      AND b.object_name = OBJECT_NAME(p.major_id)
      AND b.permission_name = p.permission_name
  );
GO

-- 10. Generate Summary Report
PRINT '\n10. Recovery Validation Summary';
GO

DECLARE @IssueCount INT;
SELECT @IssueCount = COUNT(*) FROM (
    -- Combine all checks
    SELECT IssueType FROM (/* Query 1 results */) a
    UNION ALL
    SELECT IssueType FROM (/* Query 2 results */) b
    -- ... include all checks
) all_issues;

SELECT 
    'Recovery Validation Complete' as Summary,
    GETDATE() as ValidationTime,
    DB_NAME() as DatabaseName,
    @IssueCount as IssuesFound,
    CASE 
        WHEN @IssueCount = 0 THEN '✅ RECOVERY SUCCESSFUL'
        WHEN @IssueCount <= 5 THEN '⚠️ RECOVERY WITH MINOR ISSUES'
        ELSE '❌ RECOVERY WITH SIGNIFICANT ISSUES'
    END as RecoveryStatus,
    CASE 
        WHEN @IssueCount = 0 THEN 'Database restored successfully. All validation checks passed.'
        WHEN @IssueCount <= 5 THEN 'Database restored with minor issues. Review individual checks.'
        ELSE 'Significant issues detected. Immediate review required before production use.'
    END as Recommendations;
GO

-- Create validation log entry
INSERT INTO recovery_validation_log (
    validation_time,
    database_name,
    issues_found,
    validation_status,
    performed_by
) VALUES (
    GETDATE(),
    DB_NAME(),
    @IssueCount,
    CASE WHEN @IssueCount = 0 THEN 'SUCCESS' WHEN @IssueCount <= 5 THEN 'WARNING' ELSE 'FAILURE' END,
    SYSTEM_USER
);
GO
